The R-2 counter-program split was kept by moving the binding into the importing file as a local `let g` (imported_global) rather than silently dropping the cross-file scrutinee coverage [corrected at the W-069 plan round: this sentence previously said 're-authored to `var g`' — the interim var re-author was structurally wrong (a `var` initializes by copying, and choice types implement no Core.Copy) and was reverted within W5-S3b itself (commit ac1afa4); the tree's final S3b state is the local `let`, matching the subfile's own comment]; restoring a `let`-based split is the acceptance test for discharging this item. items.notes: Filed at W8c per the OQ-4 adjudication (fork/w008/plan.md §3.3/§5: a NEW S-size item, neither W-008 scope nor folded into W-066). `bool` scrutinees are design-reachable: pattern_matching.md:591 treats `bool` 'like a choice type' whose alternatives are `false` and `true`, so `case true`/`case false` arms dispatch by value and a match covering both needs no `default` (the SF-7 exhaustiveness machinery extends). Today a `bool` scrutinee stays behind the scrutinee gate (`match on unsupported scrutinee type`, handle_match.cpp:238), pinned by fail_todo_non_int_scrutinee.carbon's bool-scrutinee probe. Implementation rides landed machinery: admit `bool` at the gate, compare via the expression-pattern `==` lane — which requires a deliberate, recorded widening of the R9 constant-integer admission to bool constants (pattern_match.cpp:1170) — and record `true`/`false` coverage the way choice alternatives record (S2e). Interaction: if W-066 lands first, its usefulness domain should include bool constant values from the start. DISCHARGED (2026-09-26, fork/w076/plan.md, full R11 loop; both plan reviews and both implementation reviews converged/approved — the plan reviews' shared major, the positionally-global R9 widening unlocking bool constants in choice-payload positions, was folded and pinned). Mechanism: BoolType admitted at the scrutinee gate (strict singleton; adapters stay gated); the R9 admission widened to concrete BoolLiteral constants (string now '...not a constant integer or `bool`', re-pinned at its three sites); true/false coverage records 0/1 into covered_alternatives (doc updated); NEW MatchNonexhaustiveBool diagnostic (values spelled `false`/`true`); usefulness gains BoolConst keys + the step-3b union rule generalized to bool roots computed WITHOUT touching choice metadata; reused full-coverage note renders 'all alternatives of `bool`'. Fix round 1 (runner-exposed, plan-hedged): `case 1 == 1` does not parse (pattern grammar binds tighter than comparison; `case 2 + 3` parses because `+` binds tighter) — positive reshaped to `case (1 == 1)` via the W8a paren-pattern lane and the bare form pinned as fail_unparenthesized_comparison_case. Reconciliation: churn confined to the new files + the three named strips; fail_question.carbon's 44 refilled lines byte-identical except the ONE R9 message line — the strongest possible §6 evidence. items.notes: Filed at W-012 discharge (fork/w012/plan.md §8.5). F-011 reserved boolean chaining for after 0.1 (if-let.md:330-334: the grammar keeps `)` right after the initializer so a Rust-style let-chain can be added without reparsing). W-012 enforces the reservation at CHECK time, not parse time: `e and c` is a legal initializer expression and no ambient precedence excludes only `and`/`or` (LogicalAnd/LogicalOr are incomparable with As and Where, precedence.cpp), so the IfCondition/WhileCondition pattern path inspects the initializer's parse-node kind and diagnoses PatternConditionChainReserved on ShortCircuitOperatorAnd/Or roots; the parenthesized `(e and c)` passes as a ParenExpr root, and let-else initializers are not restricted. Landing chains means: parse grammar for `(let P = e and c1 and let Q = f ...)` under the pattern-condition states (PatternConditionAfterPattern), check emitting each chain link as a nested test with the bindings of earlier links in scope for later ones (the if-let scope pushed at PatternConditionIntroducer already covers the then-block), evaluation-order text extending p005545 (if-let.md open question 7), and lifting the check-time gate (its two pins flip). Design authorship is part of the item: F-011 fixed only that the grammar must not foreclose chains.

items.notes: Filed at OV-2 discharge (fork/overload/plan.md §8.5; the implementation review's MINOR 4). The candidate probe deduces a generic member non-diagnosing INSIDE the discard scope, but deduction ends in `MakeSpecific`, which runs `ResolveSpecificDecl` — the generic's declaration block is evaluated in the minted specific before the conversion loop decides whether the member is selected. For a candidate that deduction accepts and conversion rejects (the `discard_probe_constants` shape), `specifics()` keeps the specific (predicted and pinned as the extra `define`) and any diagnostic that evaluating the declaration block emits — an `impls`/`where` requirement on a parameter type failing for the deduced arguments — is emitted for a candidate the call never selects. D-OV-4 step 2(e)(a) names only the definition side effect. Mechanism: deduce without minting (split `DeduceGenericCallArguments` so the probe gets the deduced argument block and the commit mints), or mint under a suppressed emitter (the W-028 probe subsystem). Unpinned in check: a pin would have to assert the stray diagnostic.

When an impl-file `extern overload fn` does not merge into its set — because the set localized to `ErrorInst` (already diagnosed; the arm returns silently) or because its redefinition of an api-inline-defined member was rejected with `RedeclRedef` — the declaration falls through to the plain path, which creates a fresh function and, for an `extern` declaration in an impl file, emits `ExternRequiresDeclInApiFile`: a second diagnostic on an already-diagnosed declaration. items.notes: Filed at the SL-1 discharge (fork/slices/plan.md §8.5). The toolchain runs `Destroy` on every `var` unconditionally, so an `UnformedInit` `Buf` would let `var b: Core.Buf(i32);` compile and then `free()` stack garbage at scope exit — nothing in the goldens or programs executes that path, so it would have shipped green; `Buf` therefore has no `UnformedInit` impl and the declaration is refused at compile time. Mechanism: the design's 'destroy is skipped for unformed variables' rule — track the formed state of a `var` (a flag or definite-initialization analysis) and gate the cleanup's `Destroy` call on it; then `impl forall [T: Copy & Destroy] Buf(T) as UnformedInit {}` is added and `fail_unformed` is deleted. Break condition: that rule is implemented.

items.notes: Filed at the SL-1 discharge. A blanket `impl forall [U: ImplicitAs(i64)] Slice(T) as IndexWith(U)` cannot serve: for `U = IntLiteral` its `At` would call `int.convert_checked`, compile-time only, on a runtime `subscript` (the round-3 crash), and `String`'s identical impl lowers only because its `At` is a call-site-lowered builtin. Mechanism: either a second concrete `impl ... as IndexWith(i32)` pair on `Slice`/`Buf` (the int.carbon:31/:42 pair pattern; `i32 -> i64` widening is `int.convert`, runtime-capable) or a general integer-subscript widening rule in handle_index.cpp beside the literal rule (any `Int(N)` subscript with `N <= 64` converts to `i64` when the operand implements `IndexWith(i64)` only). items.notes: Filed at OV-3 discharge (fork/overload/plan.md §8.5; the implementation review's MINOR 6; id allocated after SL-1's W-108..W-116, final at the trunk merge). The Carbon-to-C++ type map is injective for the realistic cases — on LP64 `Cpp.long` IS `i64`, so that pair is a Carbon redeclaration error; return-type-only differences are rejected on the Carbon side — but naming `Core.CppCompat.Long64` explicitly beside `i64`, or `Core.Char` beside the char-literal type, yields two members whose C++ declarations have one signature. Outcome is Clang's "call to 'F' is ambiguous" at every C++ call of the set, not a crash or a duplicate-symbol error (the internal-linkage inline `F`s are emitted only when selected, and an ambiguous call selects neither); the Carbon side is unaffected. Unpinned: no golden names `Core.CppCompat.Long64` in a set. Mechanism: an `ASTContext::hasSameType` compare of each new member decl's type against the list before `push_back`, dropping the later member with a semantics TODO (or a dedicated note) naming the earlier.
